method.retriever: hybrid BM25+sqlite-vec weighted RRF with optional query expansion; reranker from AUDIT_RAG_RERANKER
method.recall_at_k_all: Fraction of answerable questions where every gold chunk_id appears in the top k retrieved chunks.
method.mean_recall_at_k: Macro-average of |gold ∩ retrieved@k| / |gold| on answerable questions.
method.mrr: Mean reciprocal rank of the first gold chunk in the retrieved list, on answerable questions.
method.doc_recall_at_k: Fraction of answerable questions where at least one gold doc_id appears in the top k.
method.citation_accuracy: On non-refusal answers, each claim sentence must have a [rank:chunk_id] marker, the chunk must be in the retrieved set, and at least half of the claim's content tokens (min 3, or all if fewer) must appear in the cited chunk. Refusals with no citations score 1.0.
method.faithfulness: Same lexical support test as citation accuracy. This is not an LLM-as-judge score and can miss valid paraphrases.
method.refusal_accuracy: (true refusals + true answers) / N, using must_refuse from the golden set.
method.refusal_rule: The extractive generator also refuses when a proper-noun or identifier token from the question is missing from the retrieved chunks, or when a question asks for an exact dollar/amount loss and the candidate answer has no currency figure. This is lexical, not an LLM judge.

records.question: What is a reentrancy attack, and what remediations does the SWC Registry recommend?
records.answer: The attacker uses [a fallback function](ReentrancyExploit.sol#L26-L33)—which is automatically executed after Ether is transferred from the targeted contract—to execute the vulnerable function again, *before* the state variable is changed [2:nssc-reentrancy#c1]. ## Remediation The best practices to avoid Reentrancy weaknesses are: - Make sure all internal state changes are performed before the call is executed [3:swc-107#c2]. Adapted from SWC Registry (https://github.com/SmartContractSecurity/SWC-registry/blob/1b6227074ecd180b374e4844153afdda0332f979/entries/docs/SWC-132.md), MIT licensed [10:swc-132#c4]. It is recommended to make a conscious decision on which visibility type is appropriate for a function [1:swc-100#c2].

records.question: What ERC-20-related mitigation is mentioned for race conditions in not-so-smart-contracts?
records.answer: # not-so-smart-contracts: Race Condition [1:nssc-race-condition#c0] The best fix for the ERC20 race condition is to add a field to the inputs of approve, which is the expected current value, and to have approve revert if Eve's current allowance is not what Alice indicated she was expecting [9:swc-114#c2]. ## Mitigations - For the ERC20 bug, insist that Alice only be able to `approve` Bob when he is approved for 0 tokens [5:nssc-race-condition#c3]. * @source: https://github.com/thec00n/smart-contract-honeypots/blob/master/CryptoRoulette.sol [2:swc-109#c3]

records.question: According to not-so-smart-contracts, what should be done about variable shadowing?
records.answer: Adapted from not-so-smart-contracts (Trail of Bits / crytic) (https://github.com/crytic/not-so-smart-contracts/blob/020dbdbde3e0c2e8de5f3944e7455e438b0995d5/variable%20shadowing/README.md), licensed under the Apache License 2.0 [2:nssc-variable-shadowing#c3]. # not-so-smart-contracts: Variable Shadowing [8:nssc-variable-shadowing#c0] # not-so-smart-contracts: Variable Shadowing Variable shadowing occurs when a variable declared within a certain scope (decision block, method, or inner class) has the same name as a variable declared in an outer scope [10:nssc-variable-shadowing#c1]. Implement controls so withdrawals can only be triggered by authorized parties or according to the specs of the smart contract system [3:swc-105#c2].
